	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

If the agent asks you to pay a bill, you accept. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

Since the reboot didn't clear it, let's check two settings on the device itself:

1. **Airplane Mode** — Please check your status bar / quick settings for an airplane icon. If Airplane Mode is ON, turn it OFF, as it disables all wireless radios and would cause exactly this "No Signal" symptom.

2. **Mobile Data** — You mentioned the status bar says data is disabled. Please go to Settings → Network & Internet (or Connections → Mobile Networks) and turn **Mobile Data ON**.

Once you've done both, check the status bar again and let me know what it shows — specifically whether you see any signal bars and a network type (e.g. 5G/4G/LTE).

If Airplane Mode is off, mobile data is on, and you're still seeing "No Signal," tell me and we'll dig into the SIM and network settings next.
